scope: Individual source review and outstanding acceptance, not execution credit.

reviews.basis: Dining philosophers is an actual synchronization coding exercise. Ordered lower/higher fork acquisition removes circular wait; try-lock release/retry is an alternative, with starvation/livelock guarantees distinct from deadlock freedom.
reviews.acceptance: Run real competing workers with exclusive fork ownership, verify eating only while owning both adjacent forks, completion and cleanup. Do not substitute a sequential eating schedule or claim fairness from a few observed schedules.

reviews.basis: A deadlock-preventing lock class accepts upfront per-owner acquisition orders only when their union dependency graph remains acyclic, then enforces the declared order for returned locks.
reviews.acceptance: Test overlapping declarations, cycle rejection/rollback without deleting another owner edge, repeated owner declarations, invalid/out-of-order acquisition, lock exclusivity and actual concurrent acquisition. A DAG boolean alone does not implement the class.

reviews.basis: Three independently started methods must execute their work in first/second/third order using synchronization, regardless of launch order.
reviews.acceptance: Start actual threads/workers in all six orders, synchronize readiness and observe work completion before the dependent method begins. Reject unsynchronized, sleep-dependent and deadlocking starters. A sorted output array is not evidence of synchronization.

reviews.basis: The concurrent FizzBuzz variant uses four workers for divisible-by-3-and-5, only-3, only-5 and remaining numbers, producing one ordered sequence.
reviews.acceptance: Execute actual four-worker coordination; verify emission role, exactly-once increasing order, n=0/end boundaries, multiple independent instances and completion. Do not replace it with QuestionA sequential FizzBuzz.
